p|panel|av_sancion_ftc_avast: According to the FTC, Avast collected the browsing history of users of its antivirus and extensions, kept it indefinitely and sold it to more than 100 companies through its subsidiary Jumpshot, while claiming to protect their privacy. The order bans it from selling or licensing browsing data for advertising and requires it to delete the data passed to Jumpshot, notify those affected and pay $16.5 million to compensate consumers.
p|panel|av_sancion_ftc_avg: The FTC order against Avast includes AVG products (same group) among those covered by the duty to notify users. It is not a second penalty: same case, same payment.
p|panel|av_sancion_uoou_avast: The Czech data protection authority fined Avast Software for processing personal data without a legal basis: it passed its users’ browsing data to its subsidiary Jumpshot, data that allowed at least some of them to be identified, and did not inform them properly. In 2025 a court upheld the breaches but annulled the amount (see the ruling).
p|panel|av_sancion_msp_avast: The Prague Municipal Court confirmed that Avast committed both breaches, but annulled the figure of about 100 million affected users and the confirmation of the amount, and sent the case back to the authority to recalculate it. Until then, the 351 million korunas are not a final amount.
p|panel|av_sancion_cma_norton: The UK competition and consumer authority investigated automatic subscription renewals. Norton undertook to let customers cancel with a pro-rata refund after renewal, to state the renewal price up front and not to present the first price as a discount. There was no fine and no admission of wrongdoing.
p|panel|av_sancion_cma_mcafee: The UK competition and consumer authority investigated automatic subscription renewals. McAfee undertook to let customers cancel with a pro-rata refund after renewal, to simplify refunds and to state the renewal price up front. There was no fine and no admission of wrongdoing.
p|panel|av_sancion_bis_kaspersky: The US Department of Commerce banned Kaspersky from selling its antivirus in the country and, from 29 September 2024, from updating it, on national-security grounds. It is not a fine, and people who keep using it commit no offence.
p|panel|av_sancion_canada_kaspersky: The Government of Canada blocked and removed Kaspersky applications from official mobile phones. It only covers government devices.
p|panel|av_sancion_bsi_kaspersky: Germany’s Federal Office for Information Security officially warned against using Kaspersky’s antivirus and recommended replacing it. It is neither a fine nor a ban. A German administrative court rejected Kaspersky’s urgent application to withdraw the warning.
p|panel|av_sancion_dhs_kaspersky: The US Department of Homeland Security ordered federal government agencies to identify and remove Kaspersky products from their systems. It only covers the federal government.

p|panel|av_mercado_lead: Many people do not know how much money the antivirus business moves or where it comes from. These figures are from official or recognized sources; each has its link.
p|panel|av_mercado_1: That is the size Gartner forecasts for the worldwide consumer security market in 2028, growing about 4 % a year.
p|panel|av_mercado_2: Gen Digital —owner of Norton, Avast, AVG and Avira— earned this in its fiscal year 2025, with 40.4 million paying customers. One company holds four of the best-known antivirus brands.
p|panel|av_mercado_3: Kaspersky earned this in 2024, its all-time record, despite being banned on US government computers.
p|panel|av_mercado_4: companies to which, according to the FTC, Avast sold through its Jumpshot subsidiary the browsing history it collected with its antivirus and its browser extensions. In June 2024, an FTC order agreed with Avast banned it from selling or licensing browsing data for advertising and made it pay $16.5 million.
p|panel|av_mercado_5: Microsoft Defender comes free inside Windows 10 and 11, so it is on almost every Windows computer in the world and is the most-used antivirus. The exact split against paid ones is not reliably published.
p|panel|av_mercado_6: In 2021, after investigating subscriptions that renew by themselves, the UK competition and consumer authority accepted undertakings from Norton and McAfee to ease cancellation and refund the pro-rata part to those who did not want to renew. There was no fine.
p|panel|av_mercado_limite: The figures change every year and companies report in different currencies and calendars; take them as the order of magnitude of the business, not as today’s exact number.

p|panel|av_vigilar_off: Off: GUARDIANA stops measuring and keeping what your antivirus sends. No block you set is undone, and DNS queries are still recorded as always.
p|panel|av_max_lead: Blocks, in the Windows firewall, every outgoing connection of the antivirus programs seen on this computer: nothing of theirs leaves. While it lasts, your antivirus also gets no updates or cloud analysis, so it protects less. One click takes it off.
p|panel|av_max_aviso: Before you go on: while the block is on, your antivirus will get no updates or cloud analysis, and it will protect less. Use it only when you want nothing of it to leave, and turn it off afterwards. If GUARDIANA stops, the block goes with it; when it starts again, it puts the block back until you remove it.

The country is the server’s and the network is that of the company that runs it: it does not mean that company uses what is sent.
